=== HYPOTHESIS ===
# p_8a3f — Marco's glasses: nightstand to desk to nightstand to coffee table; Omar's glasses: bathroom to desk to armchair

This document tracks the full-day migration of both residents' glasses, which the per-object evidence shows are among the most mobile objects in the house. Marco's glasses: at 03:00 they are on the nightstand (or occasionally the desk); by 09:00 they are at desk_b1 (he puts them on for work); they stay at the desk through 11:00; by 18:00 they are back on the nightstand (work over, taken off); at 21:00 they are on the nightstand; at 22:00 and 23:00 they are on the coffee table (he is in the living room for TV, glasses set down). On weekends: 03:00 nightstand, 07:00–08:00 bathroom shelf (later morning routine), 23:00 nightstand.

Omar's glasses are even more mobile: 03:00 nightstand; 07:00 bathroom shelf (five sightings on a weekday — his morning routine); 09:00–13:00 desk_o1 (work); 16:00 nightstand (mid-afternoon break, taken off); 18:00 desk_o1 (back to work); 21:00 armchair_l1 (evening TV, glasses on the armchair beside him); 22:00 scattered (tv_stand, armchair, coffee table — he is moving around the living room). On weekends: 03:00 nightstand, 08:00 bathroom shelf.

What sets this apart: this is the only document that gives a full multi-receptacle migration path for both pairs of glasses with time-specific blocks, rather than a single "usually at nightstand" default. It differentiates from p_2a7c (which focuses on Omar's glasses only and puts Marco's at the desk with "sometimes" chance) and from p_3d7f (which gives Omar a six-receptacle path but does not track Marco's evening coffee-table shift).

What would refute it: Marco's glasses at the bathroom shelf at 14:00 on a weekday; Omar's glasses at the nightstand at 21:00 on a weekday (they should be on the armchair); Marco's glasses at the desk at 22:00 on a weekday (they should be on the coffee table).
